what: A ceiling on the RESIDENT ESTIMATE of each year x release viewport: JS heap + ArrayBuffer backing store + GPU buffers + GPU textures (renderbuffers included), read after the welcome is entered at spawn and two forced GCs. Gated by `node tools/measure_memory.mjs --gate`; .github/workflows/chicago-4d-frame-time.yml runs it beside the still-frame gate, one job per year x viewport.
unit: bytes (MiB = 1048576). Not per machine: bytes are the page's, not the CPU's. GPU bytes are MEASURED by a WebGL allocation meter (bufferData / texImage2D / texStorage2D / renderbufferStorage, less deletes), so the total is a floor on what a phone pays, not a ceiling on it: a driver's own copies and alignment are not counted.
rule: each reading plus 10 %, rounded up to 25 MiB. The first ceilings are today's figures: they hold the line while T-2547..T-2554 bring the figures down, and each of those lowers its ceiling to its own reading by the same rule in its own PR. A parcel that adds memory argues its new number here, with its reading, in the same commit.
self_test: `node tools/measure_memory.mjs --self-test` boots /1835/ on the phone with ?keep-geometry=1 (every page array kept, as before T-2158) and must read OVER the 1835 mobile ceiling.

measured.method: published year door, welcome entered at spawn, 3 frames + 1 s, two forced GCs; heap and backing store from Runtime.getHeapUsage; GPU from a WebGL allocation meter
measured.note: five invocations on one build, one per year x viewport (1812 both in one); /1835/ mobile re-read after the never-uploaded column was added (total identical, 795.7 MB, both reads)
